correctness.rationale: For \(n\ge6\), the coherently directed rim has multipath complex \(\partial\Delta(E)\cong S^{n-2}\). The first shortcut has link \(\partial\Delta(E\setminus\{e_0,e_1\})\cong S^{n-4}\), attached nullhomotopically. The second shortcut has link \(A\cup (f_0*\Delta(U))\simeq S^{n-4}\) for adjacent starts and \(A\cup(f_0*\partial\Delta(U))\simeq S^{n-4}\vee S^{n-5}\) for nonadjacent starts. Exact source/target restrictions and the unique directed cycle involving both shortcuts establish the link formulas. The first-stage complex is \((n-4)\)-connected, and the second link has dimension at most \(n-4\); hence the actual link inclusion is nullhomotopic by cellular approximation. Cone attachments therefore give the claimed integral sphere wedges and homotopy-split inclusions. A direct face/acyclicity checker passed 90 link/Euler/inclusion cases and 114 finite-field signed boundary cases; those finite checks are corroborative only.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The one-shortcut theorem does not control the link of a second shortcut; fully bidirected polygon complexes have different arc sets and neither coincide with nor naturally retract to the two-forward-shortcut complex. General attachment identities are tools, not a computed result. No explicitly stronger covering all-two-shortcut result was found.

value.rationale: Two elementary forward shortcuts form the first interaction problem beyond the natural one-shortcut perturbation. Adjacent versus separated shortcuts produce different homology dimensions, not only a modest rank change; the additional \((n-4)\)-sphere is traced to the joint-shortcut Hamiltonian cycle. This provides a sharp, parameter-uniform homotopy and primitive persistence-inclusion classification for a natural family of cyclic directed-forest complexes.
